get_messages.name: get_messages
get_messages.description: Fetch messages in a chat or channel thread, normalised: stable `id`, `version`, ISO `at`, sender `from_id`/`from`/`is_me`, parsed `mentions` + `mentions_me`, `edited`/`deleted` flags, `reply_to` (quoted-message id), and `text` with HTML stripped, links unpacked, mentions as @Name and system events summarised. The envelope carries `cursor` (= max version) for polling, `next_start_time` (cursor + 1) and the extracted `sync_state` token. `mentions_me`/`is_me` need the captured `me_mri` var (`mcx site capture teams`); without it both read false. Note `reply_to` is the QUOTED message (properties.qtdMsgs) while `replyTo` is the channel-thread parent (parentmessageid) — different things, and the quote blockquote is stripped from `text`. Use get_messages_raw for the wire shape.

paramDocs.startTime: epoch ms — SERVER-SIDE cursor, filtered on each message's `version` (not `id`), bound INCLUSIVE. Use 1 for the beginning. To poll for new activity persist the `cursor` from a previous response (= max version) and pass `startTime = cursor + 1`. Because the filter is on `version`, this also returns edits, deletes and reaction changes to older messages. The feed is ordered by `version` desc.
paramDocs.syncState: delta token. NOTE: `_metadata.syncState` in a response is a full URL, not a token — pass the `syncState` query parameter from inside that URL. Passing the token alone pages BACKWARD (history); a correct delta replays both `startTime` and `syncState` from that URL. `startTime = cursor + 1` alone is simpler and equivalent.

"." + .f + "Z") else . end), from_id: (if $fromId == "" then null else $fromId end), from: (if (.messagetype // "") | startswith("ThreadActivity/") then "system" else (.imdisplayname // "system") end), is_me: ($me != null and $fromId == $me), type: .messagetype, mentions: $mentions, mentions_me: ($me != null and (($mentions | map(.mri)) | index($me)) != null), edited: ($p.edittime != null), deleted: ($p.deletetime != null), hard_deleted: ($p.hardDeleteTime != null), reply_to: (($p.qtdMsgs // []) | if type == "array" and length > 0 then (.[0].messageId | tostring) else null end), replyTo: .parentmessageid, time: (.composetime // .originalarrivaltime), reactions: ((.annotationsSummary // {}) | if type == "object" then (.emotions // null) else null end), text: ((.content // "") | tostring | gsub("]*schema\\.skype\\.com/Reply[^>]*>[\\s\\S]*?\\n?"; "") | gsub("]*href=\"(?[^\"]*)\"[^>]*>(?[^<]*)"; if .t == .u then .u else .t + " (" + .u + ")" end) | gsub("]*schema\\.skype\\.com/Mention[^>]*>(?[^<]*)"; "@" + .n) | gsub("]*alt=\"(?[^\"]*)\"[^>]*>"; .a) | gsub("[\\s\\S]*?(?[^<]*)[\\s\\S]*?"; "[joined: " + .t + "]") | gsub("[\\s\\S]*?(?[^<]*)[\\s\\S]*?"; "[left: " + .t + "]") | gsub("[\\s\\S]*?(?[^<]*)[\\s\\S]*?"; "[topic: " + .v + "]") | gsub("<[^>]+>"; "") | gsub(" "; " ") | gsub("&"; "&") | gsub("<"; "<") | gsub(">"; ">") | gsub("""; "\"") | gsub("'"; "'") | gsub("'"; "'") | gsub("\\s+"; " ") | sub("^\\s+"; "") | sub("\\s+$"; "")) })) as $msgs | (($msgs | map(.version) | map(select(type == "number")) | max) // null) as $cursor | { count: ($msgs | length), cursor: $cursor, next_start_time: (if $cursor == null then null else $cursor + 1 end), sync_state: (((._metadata // {}) | if type == "object" then (.syncState // "") else "" end) | tostring | (capture("syncState=(?[^&]+)")? | .t) // null), messages: $msgs } end

list_threads.name: list_threads
list_threads.description: Thread directory from the same sidebar payload as list_updates: every chat with its title and member MRIs, every channel with its display name and member count, every team with its channels. Use it to identify an unknown 19:… thread id. Members carry MRIs only — resolve names with user_fetch.

list_updates.name: list_updates
list_updates.description: Unread/recent sidebar triage (chats + channels). The x-ms-synctoken header anchors the sync window and is supplied by the captured `updatesSyncToken` var — run `mcx site capture teams --limit 2000` first. The header is dropped entirely while that var is uncaptured (which also answers whether the service tolerates omitting it). The response's own next token is surfaced as `syncToken`. Use list_threads for the full chat/channel roster.

send_message.name: send_message
send_message.description: Send a message to a chat thread. Returns { id, at } — `id` is the server message id (the response's OriginalArrivalTime, which equals the last segment of the Location header and the `id` get_messages reports). clientmessageid is auto-generated from the nanosecond epoch unless supplied. Supports @mentions (--mention) and quoted replies (--reply-to).

paramDocs.content:
required — message body, HTML wrapped in

tags, e.g. '

hello

'
paramDocs.messagetype: optional — default 'RichText/Html'. Use 'Text' for plain text.
paramDocs.clientmessageid: optional — override the auto-generated idempotency key (useful for explicit retries)
paramDocs.mention:
optional — comma-separated mention list, each item `` or `=`, e.g. '8:orgid:=User One,8:orgid:=User Two'. A display name alone cannot be accepted: name→MRI resolution needs a lookup the catalog layer cannot do, so resolve first via list_threads (chats[].members[].mri) or user_fetch. Each mention emits the matching Name in the content and the JSON-encoded properties.mentions entry. If the content contains the literal '@' that occurrence is replaced in place; otherwise the spans are prepended inside the leading

. An MRI never contains a comma; a display name containing one is not supported (use --mentions).
paramDocs.mentions: optional — escape hatch: the raw JSON-encoded STRING for properties.mentions, passed through verbatim (overrides --mention). Content must already carry matching <span … itemid="N"> tags.
paramDocs.reply-to: optional — id of the message being quoted (from get_messages `id`). Emits the schema.skype.com/Reply blockquote in the content plus properties.qtdMsgs + hasValidMsgReferences.
paramDocs.reply-to-mri: optional — MRI of the quoted message's sender (defaults to the captured me_mri var)
paramDocs.reply-to-name: optional — display name of the quoted message's sender, shown in the quote header
paramDocs.reply-to-preview: optional — quoted text preview shown inside the blockquote

")) then ($woven.html | sub("^

"; "

" + $woven.prefix)) else $woven.prefix + $woven.html end) as $mentioned | (($p.replyTo // null) | if . == null then null else tostring end) as $rid | (($p.replyToMri // $v.me_mri // "") | tostring) as $rmri | (($p.replyToName // "") | tostring) as $rname | (($p.replyToPreview // "") | tostring) as $rprev | (if $rid == null then "" else "

" + $rname + "" + "" + "

\n" end) as $quote | ($d + ($p | del(.threadId, .mention, .mentions, .replyTo, .replyToMri, .replyToName, .replyToPreview, .quoteMode)) + { content: ($quote + $mentioned), clientmessageid: (($p.clientmessageid // ((now * 1000000000) | floor)) | tostring) }) as $base | ($base + (if ($p.mentions != null) then { properties: (($base.properties // {}) + { mentions: ($p.mentions | tostring) }) } elif ($mentions | length) > 0 then { properties: (($base.properties // {}) + { mentions: ($mentions | map({ "@type": "http://schema.skype.com/Mention", itemid: .itemid, mri: .mri, mentionType: "person", displayName: .name }) | tojson) }) } else {} end)) | (if $rid == null or (($p.quoteMode // "both") == "blockquote") then . else . + { properties: ((.properties // {}) + { qtdMsgs: [{ messageId: ($rid | tonumber), sender: $rmri, time: ($rid | tonumber), message: null, validationResult: "Valid", sharedRefId: null, replyChainId: null }], hasValidMsgReferences: true }) } end)

user_fetch.name: user_fetch
user_fetch.description: Resolve MRIs to display names / profile fields. The live body is a bare JSON array of MRI STRINGS — ["8:orgid:<guid>"] — and the six isMailAddress/enableGuest/… query parameters are required; the older documented [{ mri }] object form answers 400 'Invalid Users Request', and so does [{ Mri, userType }] (that object shape belongs to the sibling users/fetchfeaturesettings endpoint, which returns feature flags rather than profiles). Normalised output; the raw response is { type, value: [...] }.

paramDocs.mri: comma-separated MRIs, e.g. '8:orgid:<guid>,8:orgid:<guid2>'. Defaults to the captured me_mri var (your own profile) when omitted.
paramDocs._body: optional — raw JSON body, bypassing the --mri template.

user_fetch.jq_input:
.params as $p | (.vars // {}) as $v
| (($p.mri // "") | tostring | if . == "" then (($v.me_mri // "") | tostring) else . end)
| split(",") | map(gsub("^\\s+|\\s+$"; "")) | map(select(length > 0))
